assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only medalist:tsukasa-akeuraji@manga#provisional-character-monograph (the canonical provisional character monograph, version 1.1, INDEPENDENT_SOURCE_FIDELITY_REVIEWED) and medalist:tsukasa-akeuraji@manga#coach-and-pupil-relationship-study (the canonical coach-and-pupil relationship study, version 1.1, with its 2026-10-14 original-language addendum) at basis_commit, both read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the Japanese manga V01-V15 (Scores 1-61) to the warm-up before the Junior Grand Prix Final free skate, combined freeze MD-FR-FB02. Official Fanbooks 01 and 02 appear in both syntheses as creator-layer supplements kept separate from story fact; no grade rests on them. The frozen readings, the seven ledgers, the readiness rows, the speech and interlocutor audit, the source-fidelity audit and the Inori Yuitsuka monograph are not curated evidence on this subject, and nothing is borrowed from them. The syntheses' confidence labels and the project's 'no operational model' readiness record are inputs, not conclusions. The animated adaptation, English editions, parody chapters and anything after Score 61 are excluded, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Evidence runs from Tsukasa Akeuraji's boyhood, told as his own V15 memory (MD-EV-V15-0020, -0035), through the V15 warm-up before the Junior Grand Prix Final free skate (December of Inori Yuitsuka's first middle-school year). His past (boyhood, the hobby circle, Yokohama under Takamine Shō, the Kago household, the national championships at twenty-four) is his knowledge at every story state, though it is disclosed to the reader across V01-V15. The assessed states run from V01 (age twenty-six, MD-EV-V01-0002) through the V15 stairwell promise (MD-EV-V15-0050, -0051). V15 is split at the afternoon vow (MD-EV-V15-0010), Kanayumi Miho's criticism that evening (MD-EV-V15-0021, -0023), the late-night formulation to Kago Kōichi (MD-EV-V15-0045), the carrying up the stairwell (MD-EV-V15-0047) and the promise. Before that evening he does not know what Inori Yuitsuka carries. The state after the promise is outside the assessed scope: the evidence records it only as an untested fork between the conduct of V09 to the V15 afternoon and the promised conduct, and no state after the warm-up is established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph gives a discriminating account of Tsukasa Akeuraji: a boyhood rule that wanting costs and costing is judged underlies his refusal of help, his debt-paying and his silence about himself (HIGH for the conduct, recorded in V01, V07-V08 and V15 before the cause was told; MODERATE-HIGH for the cause); a creed against sacrifice he never applied to himself (MD-RT-0112); an eye that is strong on bodies and blind to intent (sections 5.1, 5.6); four compatible first-person motives; named fears, including shame at being consoled (MD-CS-0190); and a self-concept with nowhere to stand except as a coach (MODERATE). It predicts his mistakes: absolute promises beside a creed that nothing is absolute, risk taken at Inori Yuitsuka's appeal or on his own ambition (MD-CS-0098, MD-SK-0045, MD-CS-0167), injuries hidden and night work on cracked ribs, and statements that run ahead of conduct. A would overclaim: the cause rests on his own memory told in one evening, the origin of his eye is unresolved, and the syntheses offer no tested rules. C would understate an account that says which factor changes his response and records where it stops.

The monograph gives Tsukasa Akeuraji's history in story time and in order of disclosure, with each telling's layer and limits (section 3), and the claim version histories of MD-CL-0010, -0004 and -0025. The relationship study gives both directions of the coach-pupil relation phase by phase (V01-V03, V04-V08, V09, V10-V12, V13-V15) with its knowledge history, and the four acts of the V15 afternoon and night are located. C would understate a causally ordered, located developmental record that names its own premature readings. A is rejected: boyhood has no ages, the V14 Yokohama chapter is weighed lower as second-hand comedy, his reason for stopping skating is unstated beyond his words, and whether the V15 change holds is untested.

The evidence records written-Japanese address and register for Tsukasa Akeuraji, not sound: 俺 and いのりさん with plain instructions and contractions to Inori Yuitsuka, keeping the polite suffix even in urgent instruction (MD-EV-V03-0007); 貴方 with formal, accountable clauses to Yodaka Jun (MD-EV-V02-0028, MD-EV-V06-0037); blunter self-reference and refusals with Kago Kōichi; curt self-deprecation before Juna. The courteous manner has an in-story origin at lower weight (a vow against Juna's example) and a fanbook origin at the creator layer. B would overclaim: the speech and interlocutor audit that owns the located contrasts and counterexamples is outside the set, the monograph says no operational rule follows, dialogue is paraphrased throughout, and no forms are given for Kago Kōichi or colleagues. D would understate the located recipient contrast.

The monograph locates recurring ordinary conduct for Tsukasa Akeuraji with a driver: refusal of money and help and self-funded purchases (MD-CS-0016, -0121, -0144), a body treated as an instrument at others' disposal and stamina spent without accounting (MD-CS-0123, -0131), exuberance at the boards checked by Hitomi Takamine and Kanayumi Miho (MD-RL-0040, MD-CS-0229), praise so free it loses value (MD-EV-V11-0009), mortification at a replay (MD-CS-0309), and laundry in the Kago household (MD-EV-V02-0032). B would overclaim: ordinary behaviour is recorded mostly in comic registers and weighed so, and nothing is known of his present family or life outside coaching (MD-OQ-V15-05). D would understate a pattern shown in conduct across four volumes.

The relationship study models the relation with Inori Yuitsuka in both directions with power and options per phase, and a knowledge history of what each knew and when. Its recurring mechanisms are bounded by counter-cases: he never punishes her concealment, takes its cost as his own failure, and until V15 manages around her instead of asking why. The monograph adds Tsukasa Akeuraji's relations by person: Hitomi Takamine corrects him; with Kago Kōichi and Meiko a debt is released in words and reversed (MD-RL-0086, -0352); he refused Takamine Shō's loan; Kōhei is the colleague who brakes; Gori and Kanayumi Miho correct him and he protests and then acts within hours (MD-RL-0315, -0347); Yodaka Jun is his origin and declared opponent. A is rejected: the monograph states that his blunter manner with Kago Kōichi, his deference to seniors and his conduct toward Hikaru Kamisaki have few independent instances, and what Hitomi Takamine now thinks of their last championship is not given.

The evidence gives Tsukasa Akeuraji's interior through his own narration (V06), memory (V15), located thoughts (that he should not have asked, MD-CS-0323; his own phrase called cowardly, MD-EV-V15-0024; no place except as a coach, MD-EV-V15-0015) and hidden reactions (MD-CS-0202). It weighs self-account against witnessed past and models the gap between his statements and his conduct as a finding in its own right. A would overclaim: memory is noted as edited on recall (MD-EV-V15-0022), the account of what he wanted is partly Kago Kōichi's diagnosis with his assent qualified by 'probably', and whether his doubt after the stairwell resolves is unshown.

Conflict conduct is located with conditions. With Inori Yuitsuka, the concealment table gives five cases and his response to each; in V13 he draws a line, is not heard, listens and tells a story (MD-RL-0311, -0312). With colleagues who correct him he protests and acts within hours. With Yodaka Jun and Hikaru Kamisaki he answers doctrine with doctrine (MD-EV-V08-0037, MD-EV-V09-0046) and leaves Hikaru Kamisaki's objection unanswered (MD-CL-0010@9). With Kago Koichi he refuses money. C would understate regularities bounded by counter-cases. A is rejected: rival-coach conflict is sampled in few scenes, and his conduct in conflict after a non-gold result once he knows what she carries is untested.

The evidence records Tsukasa Akeuraji's coaching ethic with grounds: he will forbid a harm to Inori Yuitsuka's body and will not overrule her purpose (MD-CL-0007@12, MODERATE-HIGH), grounded in V15 in his view that guidance along the safe road for a child's good serves the guardian (MD-EV-V15-0049); a creed that sacrifice makes no one strong; Takamine Sho's doctrine that supporters are participants; and Kago Kōichi's refusal to sort people into guilty and innocent. The criterion is evaluated favourably with his own reservation. B would overclaim: the deciding case, where her purpose and a harm to her cannot be separated, is named as untested; he carried her over her protest an hour before the promise; and nothing is analyzed outside coaching and his own debts. D would understate stated reasons tested against conduct across V03, V04, V11, V13 and V15.

The evidence locates play in Tsukasa Akeuraji's method, a contest in which he learns the Lutz beside her (MD-SK-0064, MD-RL-0227) and a permission to fall (MD-CS-0021), and comic registers of his exuberance, romping and mortification. It does not analyze his humour as such. C would overclaim on recurring but unanalyzed instances; E would understate play that recurs as pedagogy across V02, V07 and V10.

Two dedicated syntheses, both independently source-fidelity reviewed, cover Tsukasa Akeuraji across V01-V15 by phase and by method component, with claim tables, counterevidence and revision dependencies. B would overclaim: both route to ledger keys whose bodies, the speech and interlocutor audit and the readings are outside the set; the relationship study rests on the readings' and ledgers' paraphrases and did not inspect pages; and dialogue is paraphrased. D would understate dedicated, phase-complete coverage with located keys.

Affirmative limits are recorded: diagnoses that were wrong (the double Axel for months, MD-SK-0020; the V03 shin injury unseen, MD-RT-0073; the Suzu forecast; Daria's program, MD-EV-V15-0004), explanation that three times does not arrive (MD-RL-0226, MD-EV-V11-0024, MD-EV-V13-0039), slowness on what Inori Yuitsuka believes (MD-KN-0147), an impulsive departure that left her coachless (MD-CS-0035), and declarations in V06, V08 and V13 that coexisted with contrary conduct. C would understate located countercases that bound each mechanism.

Claims carry event keys and claim versions; story time and disclosure order are separated; the knowledge history dates what each party knew; and V15 is resolved into the afternoon, evening, night and stairwell. A is rejected: the boyhood is undated, some Yokohama intervals are approximate, and the eight months of his absence before V10 are reported rather than shown.

conditions: Illustrative textual Japanese only, never quotation: toward Inori Yuitsuka, 俺 and いのりさん with plain instructions and contractions, the polite suffix kept under pressure; toward Yodaka Jun, 貴方 with formal accountable clauses.
Courteous address does not mean agreement or deference; explanation with a scoring reason for each refusal is his default manner with Inori Yuitsuka.
No lines toward Kago Kōichi, colleagues or other skaters beyond their described manner; no catchphrase or verbal tic is invented.
No acoustic or anime performance, and no line set after the V15 stairwell promise.
scenario_readiness.note: Located address and register constrain short illustrative lines from Tsukasa Akeuraji to Inori Yuitsuka and Yodaka Jun. The uncurated speech audit and paraphrased dialogue keep the use narrow.

conditions: Predictions are limited to the established mechanisms: forbid a harm to a pupil's body but not overrule her purpose; yield competitive risk at her appeal or his own ambition; explanation first and a frame, game or story when explanation does not arrive; refusal of help for himself while borrowing technical knowledge; counting a pupil's loss as his own failure and paring himself afterwards; taking his own declaration as a settlement.
His knowledge is set by the selected state: before the V15 evening he does not know what Inori Yuitsuka carries.
His diagnosis is reliable for bodies in motion and not for what a skater intends.
Whether the stairwell promise governs his conduct after a result is never resolved; no free-skate result or anything after Score 61 is generated.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One explicitly selected state from V01 through the V15 stairwell: V01-V03; V04-V08 (V08 before or after the layout reversal, MD-CS-0167); V09 (before or after the resolve never again to make her ask, MD-EV-V09-0017); V10-V12; V13 before or after the bench (MD-EV-V13-0042-0045); V14; or V15 at the afternoon vow, after Kanayumi Miho's criticism, or at the stairwell. The post-promise state is excluded.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Inori Yuitsuka as his pupil; Hitomi Takamine, Kōhei, Kanayumi Miho or Gori as the sampled colleagues; Kago Kōichi as the sampled benefactor. Transfer to a comparable child pupil is a separate, lower-confidence condition resting only on his stated practice and the Rio episode; any other interlocutor is excluded.
setting_constraints: Figure-skating training, competition, travel and the Kago household of the kinds shown.
No federation politics, technical claims beyond those the evidence attests, or ice-show career.
No resolution of the V15 fork after a result of either colour.

scenario_readiness.note: The evidence supports bounded extrapolation for Tsukasa Akeuraji in sampled coaching situations at a selected state through the stairwell. Its own refusal to choose his conduct after the promise excludes that state.

conditions: Sampled settings only: off-ice moments with Inori Yuitsuka around training and travel, the Kago household, and meetings with former clubmates such as Juna.
Exuberance, free praise, refusal of money or help, and self-funded effort are the attested patterns; comic registers are evidence of habit, not scripts.
No present family, private life, romance or leisure outside coaching is generated.
scenario_readiness.note: Located ordinary conduct supports narrow extrapolation for Tsukasa Akeuraji in the settings the monograph samples.

conditions: Coaching decisions about a pupil only: a harm to her body may be forbidden with a stated reason; her stated purpose is not overruled; options are set out with reasons.
His exceptions run toward risk at her appeal or on his ambition, and absolute promises recur.
A case where her purpose and a harm to her cannot be separated is presented as unresolved.
No ethical reasoning outside coaching and his own debts is generated.
scenario_readiness.note: The criterion Tsukasa Akeuraji applies, and his stated ground for it, support bounded deliberation in coaching decisions. Its deciding case is untested.
Neither synthesis analyzes any romance of Tsukasa Akeuraji, including with his former partner Hitomi Takamine, whose present view is not given. Nothing is established, so no readiness is claimed.

conditions: Sampled coaching functions only: technical diagnosis of a body in motion; allocation weighted to edges, steps and spins; borrowed jump instruction and harness work; rationed attempts after growth; division of the adults' functions; competition decisions at the boards.
His errors are part of the model: wrong on causes he has not been told, slow on what a pupil believes, and prone to risk at her appeal.
No post-Score-61 results, no federation politics, and no performance career are generated.
scenario_readiness.note: Coaching is Tsukasa Akeuraji's working context, and the monograph separates diagnosis, pedagogy, perception, decisions and responses densely enough for bounded extrapolation at a selected state.

known_limits.statement: The boundary for Tsukasa Akeuraji falls between the V15 stairwell promise and its first test, in the warm-up before the Junior Grand Prix Final free skate (MD-FR-FB02, Score 61). Any rule for his conduct after a result would have to choose between the conduct of V09 to the V15 afternoon and the promised conduct, and the evidence cannot choose (MD-RD-0073). The post-promise state is excluded from this assessment's scope.

The monograph states that Tsukasa Akeuraji's conduct is strongly conditioned on what he knows, and that what he knows changed more in one V15 evening than in the previous six volumes; rules fitted to the earlier man do not transfer to the man who knows what Inori Yuitsuka carries.

Tsukasa Akeuraji's first-person declarations in V06, V08 and V13 each coexisted with contrary conduct, and the readings several times took his statement for a settlement; a stated intention is never treated as predicted conduct.

Tsukasa Akeuraji's boyhood, the hobby circle and his motive for skating are his own recollection, first told in one evening under Kanayumi Miho's prompt; the corpus holds them as HIGH that he remembers so and no higher, and the link between his father's sentence and his reason for skating is the reading's inference.
His blunter manner with Kago Kōichi, his deference to seniors and his conduct toward Hikaru Kamisaki have few independent instances; several panels of one scene are one context.

Two readings of the V15 carrying up the stairwell are available, the old devotion persisting against her protest or an ordinary precaution, and the evidence does not choose (MD-EV-V15-0047, MD-VF-0144).

Both curated syntheses explicitly offer no operational model of Tsukasa Akeuraji, and the project's readiness rows record a bounded provisional monograph (MD-RD-0073, MD-RD-0078). Any conditional rule used under this record is the evaluator's bounded extrapolation from the stated mechanisms, not a project rule.

Official Fanbook 01 and 02 material, including the author's statement that he gave up the skater's road for Inori Yuitsuka's sake and the brothers' data sheet, is creator-layer context; no trait or grade in this record rests on it.

The relationship study rests on the readings' and ledgers' paraphrases and did not inspect pages; both syntheses route to ledger keys whose bodies, together with the speech and interlocutor audit and the source-fidelity audit, are outside this evidence set.

Nothing is known of Tsukasa Akeuraji's present family beyond a sentence that there is no home to go back to (MD-EV-V15-0030, MD-OQ-V15-05), and ordinary behaviour is recorded mostly in comic registers.
No held-out validation, probe set or speech census is part of the curated evidence; generated dialogue is illustrative and its accuracy is untested.
